defects.what: The `incomplete` statement ("The author stopped writing mid-thought, or left a TODO or [name] marker unfilled.") does not separate, and nothing on the page says so. I measured it four ways on a draft that literally stops mid-clause ("Rolled back the relay because the signature check was rejecting v1 payloads and the"): batched 1%, solo 1%, draft-only with no channel header 0%, three alternative wordings 2-11%. On "Hi [name], thanks for the ticket. The root cause is TODO - I'll fill this in once Priya" it reads 33-44%, still under the 0.6 bar. So the `looks unfinished` warn rule in decide() is dead, and the chip reads ~0% on every mid-typing draft - the state this demo is in almost all the time, since it judges every typing pause. smoke.mjs already prints `incomplete 0% .. 3%` across all 13 drafts and no seed draft exercises it, so nothing caught it. The page discloses the identical weakness for `misfit` in three paragraphs but stays silent about this one, so a visitor sees a confident wrong percentage. Hints are not the fix: I ran the brief's own hint pair and it saturates to 93-98% on complete drafts too, confirming the builder's no-hints finding.
defects.fix: Answer it in code, the pattern the port already established for isAuthorContact(): in data.ts add `export const looksIncomplete = (d: string) => /\\b(TODO|FIXME)\\b|\\[[a-z ]{2,20}\\]/i.test(d) || !/[.!?"')\\]]\\s*$/.test(d.trim());`, drive the `looks unfinished` rule and the chip from it, label the chip as code-derived the way the AUTHOR carve-out is, and add two TUNING_DRAFTS (one cut off mid-clause, one short but complete) so smoke.mjs regresses it. If you keep it model-side instead, disclose it in src/pages/send-guard.astro in the same terms used for `misfit` and delete the dead rule from decide().

defects.what: `misfit` is confirmed dead, as the page admits. On my adversarial draft "Jordan from Acme is escalating ticket 4821 again and frankly their IT team cannot follow a two-step guide..." posted to #public-community the guard says "Looks good": misfit 3%, /classify warn 0.54 (under the 0.6 escalation bar), everything else quiet. The chip shows "fits audience 97%" on a draft that names a customer and disparages them where anyone on the internet can read it. I tried three further wordings ("belongs in a different channel", "the people described in the audience line should not be reading this", "a manager would object") - all read 2-15% on the misfit and 5-32% on benign drafts, so no separation there either. Minor only because src/pages/send-guard.astro discloses it at length and says the audience judgment is really carried by the leak statements.
defects.fix: Either accept and keep the disclosure, or replace the single statement with two concrete ones that name what is at stake - "This draft names a specific customer or their support case." and "This draft discusses a customer's problem in a channel that is not that customer's channel." - and warn when both fire in a public or external channel. Re-measure against the polite refusal and the release note before wiring it to a rule.

defects.what: The replay table almost never carries the legal reading. The wait loop at line ~255 exits as soon as `gRef.current.judgedDraft === sc.draft && !inflight`, which happens ~1.0-1.4 s after the last keystroke, while the settle /rate only fires at SETTLE_MS = 1500 ms. So `cur.legalDraft === sc.draft` is false and decide() is called with `legal: null`, meaning the "severe legal/compliance risk" reason smoke.mjs prints for the pasted key and the customer-contact-details drafts can never appear in the on-page replay. The verdicts still land because other hard rules cover those two drafts, so it reads as correct while silently running a weaker policy than the notes describe.
defects.fix: Extend the wait condition to `gRef.current.judgedDraft !== sc.draft || gRef.current.inflight || gRef.current.legalDraft !== sc.draft`, keeping the existing 5000 ms cap so a slow /rate cannot stall the replay.

defects.what: The replay's REPLAY_MAX_MS = 60_000 deadline can overrun by about 5.7 s. When the deadline trips inside the character loop the code breaks out, but `if (stopReplay.current) break;` is false, so it still runs the up-to-5000 ms judge wait, records a row and sleeps 700 ms before the outer loop re-checks. The contract still holds because the loop is also bounded by 7 scenarios, but the wall clock the page advertises ("stops after the last one, or after 60 s") is not the one it keeps.
defects.fix: After the character loop, change the guard to `if (stopReplay.current || performance.now() > deadline) break;` so a deadline trip exits immediately.

defects.what: The original policy.ts had `legalWarn = 1.4 -> warn "legal/compliance risk"`. The port drops that rule (THRESHOLDS keeps only legalBlock) without saying so in the notes. Dropping it is the right call - /rate returns level 2 "material" on plainly ordinary drafts (the plain signature block 1.91, the author's own contact details 1.48-1.64, my hedging apology, my hostile-internal reply) - but the chip still paints amber at `g.legal >= 2`. The demo therefore shows "legal risk: material" in amber next to a verdict of "Looks good" on a benign draft, contradicting itself.
defects.fix: Either raise the chip's amber bar to level 3 to match the policy, or add one line to the Call C section of src/pages/send-guard.astro saying the original legalWarn rule was dropped because /rate reads material on ordinary business messages, and that the chip is the reading rather than a gate - the same framing already used for the misfit chip.

defects.what: Two of the original's seven sidebar channels are missing. jev-experiments/send-guard/src/lib/channels.ts exports CHANNELS (4 judged) plus DECOR_CHANNELS (#random, #support-escalations) = 7, and the brief's data_files entry names "7 channels". The port ships 5 (the 4 judged plus #general). The sidebar reads thinner than the workspace it imitates.
defects.fix: Add #random (internal, 198 members) and #support-escalations (internal, private, 23 members, topic "SEV tickets only") to CHANNELS in data.ts with an empty SEED entry each; both are audience:"internal", so no policy or prompt change is needed.

defects.what: Tone is an ordinal judgment sent as three yes/no statements instead of /rate, against the contract rule "ordinal judgments are /rate with a low-to-high scale" and against the brief's dm1_mapping, which routes tone to /rate on settle with the yes/no trio only as the typing-time proxy. Minor rather than major because the swap is deliberate, is disclosed in the Call C section of the astro page together with the way back, is cheaper on a shared key, and does reach all four levels on real drafts (warm 92% on the ship-date draft, curt 80-87% on the hostile ones).
defects.fix: Send tone as a second /rate call alongside the legal one at SETTLE_MS - `rateMany([judgeText(ch, text)], TONE_SCALE)` with the four-level warm/neutral/curt/hostile scale - let it overwrite the chip when it lands, and keep the yes/no trio as the typing-time proxy exactly as the brief describes.

defects.what: The error banner survives an emptied composer. The empty-draft branch of the useGuard effect does `setG(s => ({ ...EMPTY, calls: s.calls, samples: s.samples, error: s.error }))`, so a one-off 429 leaves a red "...keep typing to retry" line under an empty composer until the next successful judgment. Cosmetic; the UI stays usable.
defects.fix: Drop `error: s.error` from that reset so clearing the draft clears the error too.

notes:
Verified origin/demo/send-guard @ 8a0647c in an isolated worktree (checked out as local branch `verify-send-guard`; `demo/send-guard` was already claimed by another worktree). Nothing modified or pushed; three temporary probe scripts I wrote were deleted and `git status` is clean.

BUILD: `pnpm build` passes with zero errors, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. dist/send-guard/index.html exists with title "Send Guard . milliseconds.ai demos", and dist/index.html lists the demo.

SMOKE: `node src/demos/send-guard/smoke.mjs` runs against the live API and prints 13/13 - policy 7/7 on the seed scenarios against a regex-only DLP baseline of 3/7, and 6/6 on the tuning regressions. 39 calls, model time p50 36 ms, round trip p50 327 ms, 16,579 input tokens. The answers on the seed data are right for the demo's purpose: the pasted key blocks on the span read, the guaranteed ship date warns, the polite refusal sends, the hostile reply blocks, the pricing leak blocks on `confidential` 92%, the release note sends, the customer's contact details block on `pii` 95%.

ADVERSARIAL (six of my own plus a wording sweep). Passed: a credential written in prose with no regex span at all (secret 77% -> block, while regex-only DLP says send - the demo's whole pitch, working); heavy hedging (96% -> warn); the hostile reply moved into #eng-internal (curt tone -> warn, not block, the audience sensitivity the original policy had). The brief's headline risk is genuinely handled: the identical pricing-leak text reads `confidential` 92% in #customer-acme and 17% in #eng-internal, so the audience clause in the text really does carry the premise Jev read from state. Failed: the two statements in the defect list.

CONTRACT: every point holds. Files and shapes are right, demo.css is fully scoped under .d-send-guard (I checked every top-level and nested selector - the only unscoped rules are two @media wrappers), the astro page renders Demo + Island client:only + a notes slot with an unusually thorough How it works. No fetch outside src/lib/dm1.ts, no localStorage, no server code, no new dependencies, only src/demos/send-guard/ and src/pages/send-guard.astro touched. The .metrics strip carries calls, inferenceMs p50, wallMs p50/p95, judgments/s and tokens. Dm1Error renders inline in .error and the Send button falls back to "Send anyway" instead of sitting disabled. Nothing fires on load (the useGuard effect early-returns on an empty draft) and the seeded workspace renders immediately. Replay is start/stop and bounded by 7 scenarios plus a 60 s wall clock. Tokens, fonts and .panel/.btn/.tag/.metrics all come from the site stylesheets.

One deliberate deviation I checked rather than took on trust: call A goes out with no when_true/when_false hints. I ran the brief's own hint pair on five drafts and it saturates to 87-98% on complete and benign drafts alike, so the builder's measured claim is correct and omitting the hints is the right call, not a shortcut.

FIDELITY: all ten core questions plus the per-span question are ported, the interaction loop is the same (type -> pause -> judge -> green/amber/red Send with the mirrored underline layer and reason line), and the guard pane keeps the verdict cards, chips, span list, regex-DLP toggle, latency histogram and replay table. Scenarios are a superset (7 = the original 6 plus a customer-contact-details block). Reductions: 5 sidebar channels instead of 7, no Shell top bar or workspace rail, and the AbortController the brief asked to keep is replaced by a busy/dirty gate that suppresses stale pauses instead of cancelling them - quota-friendlier, but the original's "cancelled" counter goes with it.

pass=false rests on the single major: the `incomplete` chip reads ~0% on exactly the drafts this demo spends its life judging, and unlike the equally weak `misfit` chip it ships with no disclosure. Everything else is minor. Fix that one - three lines of code, following the port's own isAuthorContact() precedent - and this branch is ready.
